newsitem.title: USA: Pathmark Stores cuts 225-250 administrative jobs.
newsitem.headline: Pathmark Stores cuts 225-250 administrative jobs.

text.p: Pathmark Stores Inc said it cut 25 percent of its adminstrative staff located at its corporate headquarters in Woodbridge, New Jersey.

"We had a restructuring in which 25 percent of headquarter staff was eliminated ... this affected between 225 and 250 administrative positions," said Stan Sorkin, Vice President of Public Affairs at Pathmark.
Sorkin denied talk that Pathmark was slashing even more of its workforce, adding that none of the positions at Pathmark's 144 stores was affected.

"Two thirds of the total were either early retirement positions or jobs not currently filled in headquarters," Sorkin said. "The restructuring was implemented to help the company lower rate costs and to better meet current business needs."
Asked if he saw more cuts in its workforce or store closings going forward, Sorkin replied, "At this time no, but we will continue to evaluate the business based upon changing business conditions."
Corporate bond traders said Pathmark debt was better bid and unchanged to slightly higher on the day.
In December, Standard & Poor's revised Pathmark's outlook to negative from stable, citing lower-than-anticipated operating results during the first three quarters of 1996 and increased competition.

S&P noted, "Competition continues to be intense in several of Pathmark's markets, particularly in the Philadelphia metropolitan region where both Acme Markets, the market leader, and Giant Food Inc have aggressively opened new stores and/or stepped up their renovations of older locations."
Still, S&P affirmed the company's B-minus senior subordinated notes and debentures.

Moody's Investors Service cut Pathmark's and its ultimate parent, Supermarkets General Holdings Corp, in December, reflecting weaker-than-expected performance, fierce competition and a heavy debt load.
Moody's cut Pathmark's senior subordinated debt to B3 from B2, while shaving parent Supermarkets General subordinated debt to Caa from B3.
